blocks.recap_md: Gatsby's parties abruptly stop and he fires all his old servants, replacing them with new ones who won't gossip about Daisy's frequent afternoon visits, then invites Nick to lunch at Daisy's house.
On the hottest day of the summer, Nick takes a stifling train into the city and arrives with Gatsby at the Buchanans', where Daisy and Jordan lie motionless on a couch in the shaded, cooled room.
While waiting for Tom, Jordan whispers that Tom's mistress is on the phone, and once Tom leaves the room again, Daisy openly kisses Gatsby and declares her love for him in front of Nick and Jordan.
Daisy's young daughter Pammy is brought in and shown off to the group, and Gatsby watches her with surprise, as if he had never quite believed she existed.

Over lunch, as Daisy grows morose about the heat and the future, she stares openly at Gatsby and tells him he 'always looks so cool,' and Tom, watching, realizes with astonishment that his wife loves Gatsby.
While the group prepares to leave for town, Gatsby tells Nick that Daisy's voice is 'full of money,' and the group arranges to split into two cars, with Daisy riding to town with Gatsby.
In the car to New York, Tom - now suspicious of Gatsby and Daisy - interrogates Nick and Jordan and boasts of having investigated Gatsby's past, mocking the claim that Gatsby is 'an Oxford man.'
Stopping for gas at Wilson's garage, the group finds George Wilson sick and desperate for money, since he has decided he and Myrtle need to move out West.

Nick reflects that Wilson has just discovered Myrtle has a secret life apart from him, and as they drive off, Myrtle is seen watching jealously from an upstairs window, mistaking Jordan for Tom's wife.
Tom, panicked at the thought of losing both his wife and his mistress in the same afternoon, races to catch up with Daisy's car, and the group agrees to regroup at the Plaza Hotel.
The group takes a stifling suite at the Plaza Hotel, where tension builds as Gatsby tells Tom to leave Daisy alone and Tom mocks Gatsby's habitual phrase 'old sport.'
As wedding music drifts up from a ballroom below, Daisy and Jordan reminisce about Daisy's wedding in Louisville and a minor comic mystery about a man named Biloxi.
Pressed again about Oxford, Gatsby finally explains that he really did study there for five months in 1919, through a postwar program offered to some army officers.
Tom demands to know what Gatsby is trying to start, delivers a bigoted tirade about intermarriage, and Gatsby responds by declaring outright that Daisy never loved Tom and loves only him.
Gatsby claims that he and Daisy have secretly loved each other for five years, and under pressure from both men, Daisy reluctantly tells Tom that she never loved him.
When Tom presses Daisy about specific shared memories, she breaks down and admits she loved Gatsby once but loved Tom too, devastating Gatsby's belief that Daisy never loved anyone but him.

Tom exposes Gatsby's illegal business with Meyer Wolfshiem selling grain alcohol through fronts called drugstores, and, with Daisy now emotionally withdrawn from him, sends her home with Gatsby, confident their affair is over.
Driving back with Tom and Jordan, Nick realizes it is his thirtieth birthday and reflects unhappily on the decade of life stretching ahead of him.

At the inquest, the witness Michaelis testifies that Wilson had locked Myrtle upstairs, planning to move away, before she broke free, ran into the road, and was struck and killed instantly by a car that did not stop.
Arriving at the scene of Myrtle's death, Tom, Nick, and Jordan find her body laid out in the garage while a distraught Wilson wails, and witnesses describe the fatal car as a big, new, yellow one.
Tom quietly lies to the shattered Wilson, denying that the yellow car he drove that afternoon was his own, and once they are away from the crowd he breaks down sobbing over Myrtle's death.
Back at the Buchanans' house, Tom calmly arranges a taxi for Nick, who declines to go inside and, exhausted by the day, rebuffs Jordan when she lingers to ask him to stay.
Waiting outside, Nick is startled by Gatsby, who anxiously asks whether Myrtle was killed and reveals he has already told Daisy, believing it better the shock come all at once.
Gatsby admits to Nick that Daisy, not himself, was actually driving the car that killed Myrtle, and that he intends to take the blame to protect her.
Sneaking up to a window, Nick sees Tom and Daisy sitting together over untouched food, talking intimately like conspirators, and leaves Gatsby standing watch outside the house alone in the moonlight.

knowledge_items.statement: Gatsby dismissed every one of his old servants and replaced them with a new staff who would not gossip, because Daisy had been coming over often in the afternoons.
When Nick and Gatsby arrive at the Buchanans', Daisy and Jordan are found lying motionless on a couch in the cooled, shadowed room, complaining that the heat makes them unable to move.
While Tom is out of the room getting drinks, Daisy kisses Gatsby and tells him, 'You know I love you,' in front of Nick and Jordan.
When Daisy's young daughter Pammy is brought in and shown off, Gatsby keeps looking at her with surprise, as Nick notes he had probably never really believed in the child's existence before.
At lunch, Daisy stares at Gatsby and repeats that he 'always looks so cool'; Tom sees this and, astounded, realizes for the first time that Daisy loves Gatsby.
As they wait to leave for town, Gatsby tells Nick that 'Her voice is full of money' - the realization that finally explains, for Nick, the irresistible charm of Daisy's voice.
In the car, Tom - having just realized Daisy loves Gatsby - reveals he has made 'a small investigation' into Gatsby's past and mocks the idea, raised by Jordan, that Gatsby is 'an Oxford man.'
At the garage, a visibly sick George Wilson tells Tom he needs money because he and Myrtle are planning to move out West, news that startles Tom since it threatens to take his mistress away.
As they leave the garage, Myrtle watches from an upstairs window, but Nick realizes her jealous, frightened stare is fixed not on Tom but on Jordan Baker, whom she mistakes for Tom's wife.
At the Plaza Hotel suite, Gatsby tells Tom, 'Why not let her alone, old sport?' and Tom retaliates by mocking Gatsby's habitual catchphrase, demanding, 'Where'd you pick that up?'

Pressed by Tom about Oxford, Gatsby finally explains that he really did attend Oxford for five months in 1919, as part of a postwar program that let some army officers study at English or French universities.
When Tom demands to know 'what kind of a row' Gatsby is causing, Gatsby finally declares outright that Daisy 'never loved' Tom and 'loves' only him.

Gatsby says that he and Daisy have secretly loved each other for five years without Tom knowing; under pressure from both men, Daisy tells Tom, 'I never loved him,' though only with visible reluctance.
Pressed further by Tom about specific shared memories, Daisy finally admits the truth is more complicated than a flat denial: 'I did love him once - but I loved you too.'

Tom reveals he has investigated Gatsby's business with Meyer Wolfshiem, exposing that Gatsby's 'drugstores' were a front for illegally selling grain alcohol, and that Gatsby let his associate Walter Chase go to jail while he himself stayed clear.
As they drive back from the city after the confrontation, Nick realizes it is his thirtieth birthday and reflects gloomily on 'the promise of a decade of loneliness' ahead of him.

At the inquest, Michaelis testifies that Wilson had locked Myrtle in a room upstairs, planning to move away with her in two days, and that Myrtle later broke free, ran into the road, and was struck and instantly killed by a car that did not stop.
At the scene of Myrtle's death, witnesses describe the hit-and-run vehicle as a big, new, yellow car, matching the description of the car Gatsby had been driving that afternoon.

Tom quietly tells the grief-stricken Wilson that the yellow car he was driving that afternoon 'wasn't mine' and that he 'hasn't seen it all afternoon' - a lie, since it was Gatsby's car - though once clear of the crowd, Tom breaks down sobbing over Myrtle's death.
Waiting outside the Buchanans' house, Gatsby tells Nick he already suspected Myrtle was killed and had already told Daisy, believing 'it's better that the shock should all come at once.'
Gatsby reveals to Nick that it was actually Daisy driving at the moment of the accident, and that he intends to claim he was the one driving in order to protect her.

Peering through a pantry window, Nick sees Tom and Daisy sitting together over an untouched plate of cold chicken, talking intently in a way that gives 'an unmistakable air of natural intimacy,' as if they were conspiring together.

questions.prompt: Why does Gatsby say he fired all of his old servants and hired new ones?
options: He suspected the old staff had been stealing from him
He wanted servants who wouldn't gossip, because Daisy visits often in the afternoons
Wolfshiem insisted he give jobs to his own people
The old servants quit after his parties stopped
questions.explanation: Gatsby tells Nick, “I wanted somebody who wouldn’t gossip. Daisy comes over quite often—in the afternoons.” (The new servants were indeed people Wolfshiem wanted to help - but that isn't the reason Gatsby gives for firing the old ones.)

questions.prompt: How are Daisy and Jordan found when Nick and Gatsby arrive at the Buchanans' house?
options: Sipping cold drinks out on the veranda
Lying motionless on a couch in the cooled, shadowed room, saying “We can’t move”
Arguing loudly with each other about the heat
Upstairs getting dressed to go into town
questions.explanation: The room was “shadowed well with awnings… dark and cool,” and Daisy and Jordan lay on the couch; “‘We can’t move,’ they said together.”

questions.prompt: What does Daisy do while Tom is out of the room getting drinks?
options: She quietly asks Gatsby to leave before Tom returns
She kisses Gatsby and says, “You know I love you,” in front of Nick and Jordan
She warns Gatsby never to come to lunch again
She tells Jordan she plans to leave Tom that very day
questions.explanation: “She got up and went over to Gatsby and pulled his face down, kissing him on the mouth. ‘You know I love you,’ she murmured.”

questions.prompt: How does Gatsby react when Daisy's daughter Pammy is brought into the room?
options: He plays with her happily, delighted to finally meet her
He looks at her with surprise, as if he had never really believed in her existence before
He ignores her completely and keeps talking to Tom
He asks Daisy why she never mentioned having a daughter
questions.explanation: “Afterward he kept looking at the child with surprise. I don’t think he had ever really believed in its existence before.”

questions.prompt: What does Tom realize during the lunch scene, and how?
options: He overhears Daisy and Gatsby making plans to run away together
He sees Daisy stare at Gatsby and say he “always looks so cool,” and realizes with astonishment that she loves him
Jordan tells him directly that Daisy and Gatsby are having an affair
He finds a love letter from Gatsby in Daisy's handbag
questions.explanation: “She had told him that she loved him, and Tom Buchanan saw. He was astounded.”

questions.prompt: How does Gatsby explain the peculiar, enchanting quality of Daisy's voice?
options: He says it's because she was trained as a singer in her youth
He says, “Her voice is full of money” — its charm comes from the sound of wealth
He says it's because she speaks with a soft Southern accent
He says it's simply that he has always been in love with her
questions.explanation: “‘Her voice is full of money,’ he said suddenly.” Nick reflects, “That was it. I’d never understood before. It was full of money.”

questions.prompt: What does Tom reveal to Nick and Jordan while driving into town?
options: That he has already spoken to Daisy about a divorce
That he has made “a small investigation” into Gatsby's past and doubts he really went to Oxford
That he has hired a private detective to follow Gatsby every day
That Wolfshiem personally warned him to stay away from Gatsby
questions.explanation: “I’ve made a small investigation of this fellow,” Tom says, then scoffs, “Oxford, New Mexico… or something like that,” when Jordan says Gatsby is an Oxford man.

questions.prompt: Why does George Wilson say he suddenly needs money?
options: He wants to buy Tom's old car and start his own dealership
He and his wife are planning to move out West, and he wants to get her away
He owes money to Wolfshiem after a bad bet
The garage is about to be foreclosed on by the bank
questions.explanation: “I’ve been here too long. I want to get away. My wife and I want to go West… I’m going to get her away.”

questions.prompt: Who is Myrtle Wilson actually staring at with jealous terror from the upstairs window?
options: Tom, afraid he has come to end their affair
Daisy, whom she recognizes from a photograph
Jordan Baker, whom she mistakenly believes is Tom's wife
Nick, whom she suspects of spying on her
questions.explanation: “Her eyes, wide with jealous terror, were fixed not on Tom, but on Jordan Baker, whom she took to be his wife.”

questions.prompt: What does Tom mock Gatsby for, early in the confrontation at the Plaza Hotel?
options: His pink suit
His habitual phrase “old sport”
His claim to be a decorated war hero
His large yellow car
questions.explanation: “‘That’s a great expression of yours, isn’t it?’ said Tom sharply… ‘All this “old sport” business. Where’d you pick that up?’”

questions.prompt: What does Gatsby finally explain about his time at Oxford?
options: He never actually attended, and admits he lied about it
He attended for five months in 1919, through a postwar program for officers
He attended for four full years but never graduated
He attended Oxford, Mississippi, not Oxford, England
questions.explanation: “It was in nineteen-nineteen, I only stayed five months… It was an opportunity they gave to some of the officers after the armistice.”

questions.prompt: What does Gatsby finally declare to Tom in the hotel room?
options: That Daisy is planning to leave Tom for purely financial reasons
That Daisy has never loved Tom and loves only Gatsby
That he and Daisy were secretly married years ago
That Daisy asked him to confront Tom on her behalf
questions.explanation: “Your wife doesn’t love you,” said Gatsby. “She’s never loved you. She loves me.”

questions.prompt: How long does Gatsby claim he and Daisy have secretly loved each other?
options: Since before she even met Tom, though they never spoke
Five years, in secret, without Tom knowing
Only since Gatsby moved to West Egg that summer
Since their reunion at Nick's house for tea
questions.explanation: “I told you what’s been going on,” said Gatsby. “Going on for five years—and you didn’t know.”

questions.prompt: What does Daisy finally admit once Tom presses her about specific shared memories?
options: That she never loved Gatsby at all and was only humoring him
That she loved Gatsby once, but she loved Tom too
That she can no longer remember loving either of them
That she only married Tom for his money
questions.explanation: “I did love him once—but I loved you too,” Daisy sobs, which devastates Gatsby, who repeats, “You loved me too?”

questions.prompt: What does Tom expose about Gatsby's actual business dealings?
options: That Gatsby is secretly bankrupt and his mansion is mortgaged
That Gatsby and Wolfshiem's “drugstores” were a front for illegally selling grain alcohol, and that Gatsby let his associate Walter Chase go to jail
That Gatsby has been forging checks under an assumed name
That Gatsby never actually owned his mansion, just rented it
questions.explanation: “He and this Wolfshiem bought up a lot of side-street drugstores here and in Chicago and sold grain alcohol over the counter… You let him go to jail for a month over in New Jersey.”

questions.prompt: What does Nick realize about himself on the drive back from the city?
options: That he has fallen in love with Jordan and wants to marry her
That it is his thirtieth birthday, and he reflects gloomily on the decade ahead
That he wants to quit the bond business and move back West immediately
That he no longer believes anything Tom says about the confrontation
questions.explanation: “No… I just remembered that today’s my birthday.” “I was thirty. Before me stretched the portentous, menacing road of a new decade.”

questions.prompt: According to Michaelis's testimony at the inquest, what had Wilson done to Myrtle shortly before her death?
options: He had thrown her out of the house after an argument
He had locked her in a room upstairs, planning to move away with her in two days
He had sent her to stay with relatives out of town
He had forbidden her from ever leaving the garage again
questions.explanation: “I’ve got my wife locked in up there,” explained Wilson calmly. “She’s going to stay there till the day after tomorrow, and then we’re going to move away.”

questions.prompt: How do witnesses at the accident scene describe the car that struck and killed Myrtle?
options: An old, battered black car
A big, new, yellow car
A small blue coupé
A dark green delivery truck
questions.explanation: “‘It was a yellow car,’ he said, ‘big yellow car. New.’” This matches the car Gatsby had been driving.

questions.prompt: What does Tom tell the grief-stricken Wilson about the yellow car, and is it true?
options: He truthfully admits the yellow car was his own
He falsely claims the yellow car wasn't his and that he hasn't seen it all afternoon
He tells Wilson he doesn't know anything about any yellow car
He truthfully says the yellow car belongs to Gatsby
questions.explanation: “That yellow car I was driving this afternoon wasn’t mine—do you hear? I haven’t seen it all afternoon.” In fact it was Gatsby's car that Tom had driven into town.

questions.prompt: What does Gatsby tell Nick when they meet outside the Buchanans' house that night?
options: That he plans to turn himself in to the police immediately
That he already suspected Myrtle was killed and had already told Daisy about it
That he is leaving for Europe the next morning
That Tom has threatened to have him arrested
questions.explanation: “I thought so; I told Daisy I thought so. It’s better that the shock should all come at once. She stood it pretty well.”

questions.prompt: Who does Gatsby reveal was actually driving the car when it struck and killed Myrtle?
options: Gatsby himself, exactly as he told the police
Daisy, though Gatsby plans to say he was driving to protect her
Jordan Baker, who panicked and lost control
No one - Gatsby claims the car swerved on its own
questions.explanation: “Was Daisy driving?” “Yes,” he said after a moment, “but of course I’ll say I was.”

questions.prompt: What does Nick see when he sneaks up to peer through the pantry window of the Buchanans' house?
options: Daisy sobbing alone at the kitchen table
Tom and Daisy sitting together over untouched food, talking intently like conspirators
Tom packing a suitcase, preparing to leave Daisy
Daisy on the telephone, seemingly speaking to Gatsby
questions.explanation: “Daisy and Tom were sitting opposite each other at the kitchen table, with a plate of cold fried chicken between them… anybody would have said that they were conspiring together.”
